calls.title: The Tow Yard
calls.about: An existing client calls from the side of a busy road, with trucks and horns behind him.

key.v: Marcus Bell, existing client
(555) 013-4471, before 5:00 PM Eastern today
Yes: full name, DOB 04/17/1988, DOL 08/02/2026
The tow yard wants about $600 in storage fees; the property damage adjuster called him; new treatment: Bayshore Physical Therapy, twice a week, from 10/26/2026
Noted on the file; message to Mara Quintero (Case Manager) for a callback today about the storage fees, the adjuster and the new treatment

calls.handled: Asked him to step away from the road, read the callback number back slowly when a truck covered it, and repeated every detail back.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Rina. How may I help you today?
Yeah, hi, this is Marcus Bell, I'm a client there. Sorry, I'm, uh, I'm at the tow yard on Hillsborough, it's loud out here.
That's all right, Mr. Bell. I'm having a little trouble hearing you over the traffic. If you can, could you step away from the road for a moment, or cup the phone?
Hang on. Hang on.
Okay. Is that better?
Much better, thank you. Before we go on, I just need to verify your file. Can you give me your full name, your date of birth, and the date of the accident?
Marcus Bell. B, E, L, L. Birthday is April seventeenth, nineteen eighty-eight. And the accident was August second. This year.
Thank you. That's Marcus Bell, date of birth April seventeen, nineteen eighty-eight, and the accident on August second, twenty twenty-six. You're verified. What can I help you with today?

So two things. They finally released my car, but the tow place is saying I owe like six hundred dollars in storage fees. And the property damage adjuster called me yesterday, I didn't pick up. I don't know if I'm supposed to talk to him.
I understand. So the tow yard is asking for about six hundred dollars in storage fees, and the property damage adjuster left you a message. Is that right?
Yeah. Oh, and the other thing, I started physical therapy. Bayshore Physical Therapy, twice a week. Mara said to tell you guys when I start anything new.
Thank you for letting us know. Bayshore Physical Therapy, twice a week. And when was your first visit there?
Monday. This Monday. The twenty-sixth.

Got it, Monday, October twenty-sixth. Mr. Bell, I'll send all of this to your case manager, Mara Quintero, so she can get back to you about the storage fees and the adjuster. If the adjuster calls again before then, you can take his name and number and let us know. What's the best number for Mara to reach you?
This one. Five five five, oh one three, four four seven one.
Let me read that back. Five five five, zero one three, four four seven one.
Sorry, what? A truck just went by.
No problem. Five, five, five. Zero, one, three. Four, four, seven, one.
Yep, that's it.
And is there a good time for her to call?
Anytime before five. I'm off today.
Perfect. I've noted it on your file, and Mara will call you back today, before five PM Eastern. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that's it. Thanks.
You're welcome, Mr. Bell. Stay safe out there. Goodbye.

calls.title: Breaking Up on the Highway
calls.about: A potential new client calls from her car on the interstate; the line breaks up, then drops.

key.v: Tanya Brooks, potential new client (not yet a client)
(555) 014-2290, taken first in case the call dropped
New caller: no file to verify; name spelled, DOL 10/27/2026
New auto case: hit on the driver's side by a red-light runner at Brandon Blvd & Kings Ave; neck and left wrist injuries; ER on 10/27, now going to urgent care
Called her back after the drop; priority callback from the Intake Team (ext. 600) within the hour

calls.handled: Took the name and callback number first, asked for only the digits it missed, and called back at once when the call dropped.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Paolo. How may I help you today?
Hi, um, I was in an accident yesterday and somebody told me I should call a lawyer, so I'm, I'm calling you guys.
I'm sorry to hear about your accident. I'm here to help. Your line is breaking up a little, so in case we get disconnected, can I get your name and a callback number first?
Yeah, it's Tanya Brooks, and my number is five five five, oh one four...
...two nine oh.
I'm sorry, Ms. Brooks, I missed the middle of that. I have five five five, zero one four, and then two nine zero. Could you give me the last four digits again?
Two two nine zero. Two, two, nine, zero.
Thank you. Five five five, zero one four, two two nine zero. And that's Tanya Brooks. Could you spell your last name for me?
B, R, O, O, K, S. I'm driving to urgent care right now, my neck is... my neck is really...
[the call drops]
Hello? Ms. Brooks? ... Hello?
I lost her. I'll call her back on the number she gave.
[the VA calls back]
Hello?
Hi, Ms. Brooks, this is Paolo from Harbor and Pine Injury Law. We got disconnected. Is now still a good time, or would you like us to call you once you've parked?
Oh, thank you. I'm, I'm almost there. You can go ahead.
Thank you. Just a few quick details. What date was the accident, and where did it happen?
Yesterday. October twenty-seventh. At Brandon Boulevard and Kings Avenue. Somebody ran the red light and hit my driver's side.
October twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six, at Brandon Boulevard and Kings. And were you hurt?
My neck and my left wrist. I went to the ER last night and they said follow up, so that's where I'm going.

I'm sorry, Ms. Brooks. Thank you for telling me. Since the line keeps cutting out, I'll have our Intake Team call you back today, within the hour, at five five five, zero one four, two two nine zero, once you're at urgent care. They'll go over everything with you. Does that work?
Yes. That works. Thank you so much.
You're welcome. Please focus on the road, and we'll talk soon. Is there anything else I can help you with right now?
No. No, that's it. Bye.
Take care, Ms. Brooks. Goodbye.

Yes: full name, DOB 03/09/1979, DOL 06/14/2026, before the transfer

Offered Spanish under the firm's rule; warm transfer to Mara Quintero (bilingual Case Manager, ext. 610), with the caller, her verification, the reason and the callback number passed on

calls.handled: Spoke slowly in short words, offered Spanish straight away, took only what was needed, and briefed Mara before putting the client through.

Hello, eh... sorry, my English is... poquito. Little. Is, eh, Harbor and Pine?
Yes, ma'am. This is Harbor and Pine Injury Law. Would you like to speak in Spanish? ¿Español?
¡Sí, sí! Español, por favor. Gracias.
Okay. We have a Spanish-speaking team member. Before I connect you, I need your name, please. Your name?
Rosa Delgado. Ro-sa. Del-ga-do.
Thank you, Ms. Delgado. And your date of birth? Birthday?
Eh... March. Nine. Nineteen... seventy-nine.
March ninth, nineteen seventy-nine. And the date of the accident? Accident?
Accidente... June. Fourteen. This year.
June fourteenth, twenty twenty-six. Thank you. And a phone number, in case we get disconnected?
Five five five... cero uno cinco... eight, eight, three, four.
Five five five, zero one five, eight eight three four?
Sí. Yes. Is a letter... a bill. From hospital. They say I pay. I am... worry.
I understand. A bill from the hospital. Please wait one moment, Ms. Delgado. One moment. I will get Mara, she speaks Spanish.
Okay. Gracias.
[on hold]
Hi Rina, it's Mara.

Hi Mara. I have Rosa Delgado on line one. She's verified: date of birth March ninth, nineteen seventy-nine, accident June fourteenth, twenty twenty-six. She prefers Spanish. She received a bill from the hospital and she's worried she has to pay it. Her callback is five five five, zero one five, eight eight three four.
Perfect, thank you. Put her through.
Ms. Delgado? Thank you for waiting. Here is Mara.
Hola, señora Delgado, habla Mara Quintero, su administradora de caso. ¿Cómo está? Cuénteme sobre la carta del hospital.
Ay, gracias a Dios. Me llegó una factura del hospital que dice que tengo que pagar mil doscientos dólares, y no sé qué hacer.
No se preocupe. No pague nada todavía. Mándeme una foto de la carta por correo electrónico y yo me encargo de llamar al hospital hoy mismo.

calls.title: The Speakerphone Echo

calls.about: A provider's billing office calls on a speakerphone in a big room: an echo, a faint voice, a lot of numbers.

A provider, not the client: the patient identified as Kevin Tran, DOB 11/30/1992; no file details discussed
Needs a signed copy of the Letter of Protection re-sent (theirs is unsigned); balance now $4,850
Noted on the file; message to Devin Shaw (Records Coordinator, ext. 640) to send the signed LOP by fax and call back within one business day

calls.handled: Asked her to take the call off speakerphone, then checked the one digit the line swallowed instead of guessing.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Paolo. How may I help you today?
Hi, good afternoon, this is Janelle with Bayview Orthopedics billing, I'm calling about a patient of ours who's one of your clients.
Good afternoon, Janelle. I'm sorry, there's quite an echo on the line and your voice is a bit faint. Are you on speakerphone? Could you pick up the handset?
Oh, sorry, yes. Hold on.
Is that any better?
That's a lot better, thank you. Which patient are you calling about?
The patient is Kevin Tran. T, R, A, N. Date of birth November thirtieth, nineteen ninety-two.
Kevin Tran, T, R, A, N, date of birth November thirtieth, nineteen ninety-two. And what can I help you with?

We need a copy of the letter of protection re-sent. The one we have on file is unsigned. And we wanted to let the case manager know his balance with us is four thousand eight hundred and fifty dollars.

Understood. A signed copy of the letter of protection, and the current balance is four thousand, eight hundred fifty dollars. I'm sorry, the line cut in and out there. Was that seven seven two zero, or seven seven two two?
Zero. Seven, seven, two, zero.

Five five five, oh one six, seven seven hundred, extension two one two.
Five five five, zero one six, seven seven zero zero, extension two one two. And your last name, Janelle?
Ortiz. O, R, T, I, Z.
Janelle Ortiz, Bayview Orthopedics billing. I've noted this on the file, and Devin will get back to you within one business day. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that's everything. Thank you, Paolo.
Thank you, Janelle. Have a good afternoon.

calls.title: Mom on the Line
calls.challenge: Background noise and an unauthorized caller
tags: Family member not on the file
calls.about: A client's mother calls from a busy house, upset: her son is back in hospital and she wants to know about his case.

key.v: Linda Carter, mother of the client Jordan Carter
Not the client and not authorized in writing: nothing shared or confirmed, not even whether there is a case
Jordan was admitted to Tampa General on 10/27/2026 after a fall (his knee); she asked when the settlement is coming
Urgent message passed on internally (to Jordan's case manager, Mara Quintero) for someone to call Jordan directly today; told Jordan can call himself to authorize her; noted on the file

calls.handled: Stayed calm and kind through the noise and the frustration, confirmed nothing about a case, said why nothing could be shared, and still took the urgent message.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Paolo. How may I help you today?
Yes, hi, my name is Linda Carter, my son Jordan is your client, and I need to know what is going on with his case, because nobody is telling us anything.
Grandma! He took my tablet!
Not now, baby! Sorry. Sorry.
That's all right, Ms. Carter. I can hear this is a stressful time. I'll do my best to help you. May I ask, are you calling on someone's behalf today?

Yes, for my son, Jordan Carter. He fell again, because of his knee, and he's back in the hospital since last night. Tampa General. And I want to know when the settlement is coming, because the bills are piling up.
I'm so sorry to hear Jordan is in the hospital. Please give me one moment.

Thank you for waiting, Ms. Carter. For privacy, we can only discuss a case with the client, or with someone the client has authorized in writing, so I'm not able to share or confirm any information. I know that's frustrating to hear.
I'm his mother! I'm the one driving him to all his appointments.

I completely understand, and I can hear how much you're doing for him. It's to protect Jordan's privacy. What I can do is take a message and pass it on right away, so the right person can reach Jordan directly. If Jordan would like you to be able to speak with us, he's welcome to call us himself, and we'll explain how.
Okay. Okay. Yes, please do that.
Grandma, the dog is out!
Thank you. What's the best number to reach you, in case she needs to?
Five five five, oh one eight, six six one two.
Five five five, zero one eight, six six one two. And so I have it right: Jordan was admitted to Tampa General last night, October twenty-seventh, after a fall, because of his knee. Is that correct?
Yes. That's right.
Thank you, Ms. Carter. I've passed your message on as urgent, and someone will reach out to Jordan today. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No. Thank you. I'm sorry I yelled.
Please don't apologize. I hope Jordan feels better soon. Take care, Ms. Carter.
